dct_description_sm: The purpose of the study was to examine the factors that influence black spruce survival and success above the current treeline in the Mealy Mountains of Labrador.  Germination and growth rate of black spruce seedlings were compared when planted on a variety of seedbeds (groundcovers) and under a series of herbivory protection levels in order to determine the relative importance of seedbed and herbivory on early black spruce success in the alpine tundra community.  The dynamics of the Mealy Mountains treeline may alter under the influence of climate change, so it is important to understand the role of biological controls in the early establishment of black spruce in alpine habitats, and how these factors may influence tree expansion.  The study seeks to evaluate the following reseach questions:   a)On which seedbeds do planted black spruce seedlings survive and establish with the highest success? b)Are bear digs an equitable microhabitat for black spruce seedlings?  c)Do seed and seedling predation occur more frequently on a particular seedbed?  What is the magnitude of this potential difference? d)      On which seedbed do black spruce seeds emerge and establish with the highest success? e)What is the relative importance of predation and seedbed factors in black spruce survival above the treeline of the Mealy Mountains?  The study will also contribute data to predictive models of potential black spruce migration above the current treeline.
dct_title_s: Black spruce recruitment in the Mealy Mountains, Labrador
